evidence: Cic. Off. 2.51: praesertim cum dē philosophiā scrīberem (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Most often with cum or sī: praesertim cum, especially as; praesertim sī, especially if. It may follow its word.

terms.gloss: most of all, above all, especially
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.33: in rē pūblicā maximē cōnservanda sunt jūra bellī (Lewis & Short)

terms.comment: In the sense “especially” (= praesertim), poetic and post-Augustan (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: omnis hīc aetās piscandī nāvigandī atque etiam natandī studiō tenētur, maximē puerī, quōs ōtium lūsusque sollicitat
phrases.english: everyone here, of every age, loves fishing, sailing and swimming too, the boys most of all, tempted by free time and play

phrases.latin: maximē autem date operam ut valeātis, sī nōs vultis valēre
phrases.english: but above all, all of you, take care to keep well, if you want me to be well

sources: Lewis & Short: praesertim · Lewis & Short: maxime · Lewis & Short: praecipue
